subject.title: Only 41 of 219 briefs name anything the registry holds, so the reckoning withholds retirement across the board
subject.text: MEASURED, not estimated. `planning/brief-target-gate.py --quiet` over the git index on 2026-09-02 partitions 219 briefs: BROKEN_TARGET 0, WAIVED 68, DECLARED 6, PROSE_CITED 35, NO_TARGET 30, FOREIGN_ONLY 2, ABSENT_ONLY 0, UNDECLARED 78. So 41 of 219 (18.7%) join the registry at all. reckon sets `join.weak` and withholds retirement claims below 50%, which means no brief can leave the remaining set however much ships, and `unjoined` - nobody has looked at this - is indistinguishable from this shipped and nothing recorded it. WHY THIS IS FILED AS A DEFECT RATHER THAN LEFT IN THE BRIEF. `a-brief-that-names-nothing-cannot-be-retired.md` could not be joined to anything, which is its own subject arriving to it: a brief that names nothing can never be retired, so the brief about that was itself unretirable and sat in `unbuilt`, the class that means somebody wrote down what should exist and it is not there. That reading was wrong - `brief-target-gate.py` exists and blocks - and the row was there because the only id the brief cited, DEF-253, belongs to another project's registry. This row is what the brief now cites, so the brief joins and is counted as the open work it is. WHAT IS ALREADY DONE AND IS NOT THIS ROW'S WORK: the citation channel exists (`reckon-sources` frontmatter), the gate blocks a NEW uncitable brief at a per-file floor, and a citation naming an id no registry holds is BROKEN_TARGET at floor 0. WHAT IS OWED HERE: the 78 UNDECLARED briefs. The remedy is deliberately NOT a bulk write - the gate's own docstring records a sibling project whose join went 6.2% to 100% while every gate stayed green, because citations written to satisfy a tool join nothing. Each of the 78 needs a person to read it and either name its targets or declare `registry-target: none` with a reason, which is decision work rather than product work.
